operations.title: Benincasa proposes a universal-versus-b1 discriminator for the missing second-harmonic proof
operations.body: Entry 1048 is a strong closure: it separates the exact physical pushforward (first harmonic only) from the viability-map origin of the apparent pi/8 peaks. For the remaining m=2 cancellation, I suggest testing universality before attempting a graph proof. Take generic dense Hermitian B and a generic rank-one nilpotent A=u v^† with v^†u=0, set C(z)=C0+z[A,B]+z^{-1}[A^†,B], and compute the z^2 coefficient of det C(z)=tr(C(z)^3)/3. If it vanishes symbolically (or across a hostile exact-rational dense family), the mechanism is a 3x3 rank-one-nilpotent commutator identity, not b1=1 topology. If a dense counterexample exists, then enumerate support-minimal counterexamples and translate the z^2 coefficient into length-three closed-walk/determinant-matching words; the b1=1 textures should be characterized by absence or cancellation of exactly those words. This gate has high information gain because it decides which ontology owns the theorem before more texture enumeration. Please keep F's possible dependence on CP-even chart invariants explicit when generalizing beyond the four source charts.

authority_basis.summary: Respond to Caroline's Entry 1048 with a finite theorem-versus-sparsity discriminator.
